newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Moslem villagers receive Serb I.D. cards.
newsitem.headline: Moslem villagers receive Serb I.D. cards.

text.p: Bosnian Serb police began issuing identification cards on Monday to Moslems living in villages in Serb territory, the United Nations said.

The villages of Jusici, Dugi Dio and Mahala, which have a Moslem population of around 600, lie on the Serb side of the former frontline area called the Zone of Separation (ZOS) between Bosnia's Moslem-Croat federation and the Serb republic.
Attempts by Moslem refugees to return to their homes in the ZOS last year caused tensions with Serb authorities until international pressure persuaded the Serbs to allow the resettlement to go ahead.

U.N. spokesman Liam McDowall said the Serb police began issuing cards to Moslems in the Dugi Dio village on Monday morning under the supervision of the international police, NATO and other organisations.
"Things are going well in Dugi Dio and by noon 22 people received their cards," he said. "The Serb police will be moving on to Jusici later on."
The ZOS is also patrolled by NATO peacekeepers, whose presence has given Moslems refugees enough confidence to resettle in a Serb-controlled area.
The U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees planned to open another bus route across the line between the federation and Serb territory as part of confidence building.
The service between Serb-held Banja Luka in northwestern Bosnia and Croat-held Drvar is due to start on Thursday.
Both communities host refugees from these towns and Croat authorities have prevented Serbs from visiting Drvar cemeteries several times last year.
The Banja Luka-Drvar is the tenth bus route organised by the UNHCR since May last year.
